findings.title: Rejected devices are cached as successfully admitted
findings.description:
Returning the store error now makes `TagDevice` part of the authentication decision, but `tagDeviceUI` inserts the device into `localCache` **before** calling `CreateOrUpdateDevice` (line 87). When the store returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, that cache entry remains. A second request with the same device ID hits the cache, returns success, and receives an anonymous identity despite the limit.

Cache only successfully admitted devices, and ensure concurrent requests for the same device cannot observe admission before the database operation succeeds. Add a regression test that repeats authentication for a rejected device and verifies both attempts are rejected.

findings.title: Requests without a device ID bypass the limit entirely
findings.description:
`Authenticate` denies access only when `TagDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. However, `TagDevice` explicitly returns success when `X-Grafana-Device-Id` is absent (`impl.go:119-121`), so anonymous requests without that client-controlled header are accepted regardless of the configured limit.

This is also reachable through ordinary frontend requests before asynchronous fingerprint initialization completes: `backend_srv.ts` adds the header only after `deviceID` becomes available.

When a positive device limit is configured, establish a device identity before granting anonymous access or apply an explicit admission policy for unidentified requests. Test authentication at capacity both with and without the header.

findings.title: Concurrent admissions can exceed the configured limit
findings.description:
The device count and subsequent insert use separate database sessions with no serialization around the admission decision. If the limit is one and the table is empty, two requests for different devices can both count zero and then both insert successfully. The same race applies across Grafana instances.

Make counting and admission atomic using a database-backed serialization strategy that works across instances; merely wrapping the existing reads and writes in a default-isolation transaction may not prevent the race. Add a concurrent admission test asserting that the number of admitted devices never exceeds the configured limit.
